$comment: Agent eval configuration. Thresholds and budgets here are fixed BEFORE a campaign's first run; a campaign refuses to resume if its identity (arms, tasks, model, prompt, caps, harness code) changed. See evals/README.md.
prompt: You are working in a Node.js project at {{cwd}} (in Git Bash: {{cwdBash}}), where the npm package pcg-ts is installed. That is your working directory. Read brief.md in this directory and do what it asks. Work only inside this directory. When you finish, the graph must be saved as graph.json in this directory.

limits.$contaminationRateMaxWhy: RESTORED to 0.5 on 2026-09-19 once v2 finished 96/96. It was raised to 1 (off) with v2 at 86/96, after the guard fired twice in a row on the same diagnosed FALSE POSITIVE. Every flag in the cluster is one bug: a heredoc piped to `node -` was named heredoc.sh whatever consumed it, so JavaScript was scanned as shell and a division or a regex literal read as a filesystem root. quarry-terraces trips it because it is the most code-heavy task. The fix is written and tested on branch v2-msys-falsepos (765a2bf), but agents/claude-code.mjs IS part of the campaign identity, so merging it before the campaign ends would strand the last slots -- and `limits` is NOT part of the identity, which is why this knob can move and that one cannot. The guard is worth having: it exists so a systematically compromised campaign stops instead of burning allowance, and earlier in this same campaign it was two GENUINE escapes (`find /` hunting the arm's own tarball) that the classifier caught correctly. What is turned off here is the halt, not the detection: per-run flagging and the one reschedule both still apply, every flag is still recorded, and the records are re-derived from their transcripts with `reclassify --write` once the fix lands. Restore 0.5 immediately after v2 finishes. Do not read a clean contamination rate in this campaign as evidence of anything until that re-derivation has run and its before/after table has been read.

gate.$comment: Defaults, used as-is by the pilot. A campaign overrides what it needs; see evals/README.md, 'The gate'. Effort thresholds are absent here on purpose — without them limb (a) is the pilot's solved-only comparison.

calibration.$comment: Picks the tasks for v2. One run per task on the baseline arm, no repeats, no gate: it says what each task COSTS, so a task that solves in nine turns (ceiling) or burns the cap without a graph (floor) is dropped before it wastes 3 x 4 slots in v2. Same sandbox, adapter, scorer, resume, limit and contamination behaviour as any campaign; `calibration.md` is written beside report.md.

calibration-reserves.$comment: Prices the two reserve tasks, so swapping one in for a saturated v2 task is a measured decision rather than a guess, and the task count stays at 8. Same shape as `calibration`: one arm, one run per task, no gate.

v2.$comment: The sensitivity campaign the pilot asked for. The pilot came back 54/54 in EVERY arm with the corpus read in 83-89% of runs including the docs-stripped one, so v2 changes two things: held-out tasks (task.json carries "campaign": "v2"), and a stripped-all arm that loses the corpus as well as the prose. THRESHOLDS ARE FIXED HERE BEFORE THE FIRST RUN and printed in the report.
v2.$taskBudgetsWhy: Calibration measured quarry-terraces at 83 turns against a budget of 100 - 20% spare, the only one of the eight under 50% (next tightest: cavern-lamps 57/120, 111%). The gate's own effort threshold is +25%, which puts a harder arm at ~104 and over the budget, so the stripped arm would produce a TRUNCATED run instead of a clean 'cost more turns' measurement - the gate would read the cap, not the effect. 130 leaves 57% spare and clears +25% with room. A task's task.json lives in the private repo; taskBudgets sets it where the campaign is defined, so the number is visible in public beside the thresholds it interacts with. The other seven are unchanged.

gate.label: v2 gate
gate.$strippedRefWhy: stripped-all is cut FROM candidate-U1, so candidate-U1 is what it answers a question about. Comparing it against A/A-prime (built from 0ad6998) would measure 'lost the docs and the corpus' and 'changed the library' as one effect: 19 shared non-doc entries differ byte-for-byte between the two tarballs, dist/index.js and package.json among them. The A/A pair is still the noise floor, which is its job in (b) and in the 'more than the A/A gap' term of (a). Both contrasts are printed in the report body: candidate-U1 vs A says whether U1 helped, stripped-all vs candidate-U1 says whether these tasks can see documentation at all.
gate.$limbCWhy: PRE-REGISTRATION CHANGE, decided 2026-09-18 from CALIBRATION evidence and committed BEFORE v2's first slot, with zero v2 data in existence. It changes what (c) MEANS; it changes no threshold. Calibration ran 10 solves in 10 attempts (8 slots plus 2 re-runs whose contamination flags were later shown spurious), 5 of them one-shot, with the cheapest solve at 23 turns. Limb (c) as first written fails any task at 100% solved across the reference arms, so it would have failed on essentially every v2 task - while the signal we actually expect from a docs-stripped arm lives in EFFORT, not in solved rate. (c) now asks whether a task can discriminate in the DIMENSION the gate is using: floor/ceiling on solved when limb (a) fired on solved, and 'the arms differ by more than the A/A effort gap' when it fired on effort. A task saturated on solved but spread on effort no longer blocks a verdict that rests on effort. Saturated tasks are still NAMED in replaceTasks, because they remain worth swapping for reserves later; they simply do not veto a result they cannot affect. When NO limb fired the gate stops regardless and (c) is only advising which tasks to replace, so it falls back to the solved question it has always asked - the pilot's behaviour, unchanged. It deliberately does NOT ask about effort there: the effort floor is the MEASURED A/A gap, which is 0 whenever the two baselines share a median (common with small integer turn counts), and a floor of 0 would call every non-identical task informative and quietly pass (c) on a campaign the old rule failed.
gate.$why: aaMaxGap and strippedMinMargin are the pilot's, unchanged: n per arm moves only from 18 to 24, so the noise argument that fixed them still holds. The effort numbers come from the pilot's own A/A pair, which is the only measurement of run-to-run wobble there is, quoted in the STATISTIC THE GATE COMPUTES: the LARGER MAGNITUDE of the two directions of the paired-by-task mean relative difference of per-task medians (larger, because a relative difference is asymmetric and the gate must not depend on the order of baselineArms). Pilot A/A: turns 4.4% (the two directions are -2.4% and +4.4%), tool calls 4.6%, output tokens 4.3%, wall minutes 9.6%. aaMaxEffortGap 0.15 sits above the widest of those and well above turns' 4.4%, so the pilot's own noise would have passed (b). CAVEAT recorded 2026-09-18: correcting the classifier (cross-call cwd, output-flag writes, and a JS regex literal read as a filesystem root) clears ALL FOUR pilot discards, and with the cleared attempts counting instead of their retries two of those four gaps move - output tokens 4.3% -> 14.0% and wall minutes 9.6% -> 13.5%, while TURNS AND TOOL CALLS DO NOT MOVE AT ALL (4.4% and 4.6%). The gate's effortMetric is turns, so neither threshold is affected whichever way the pilot records are finally settled; what changes is the headroom in the justification, from 'the widest gap is 9.6% against a 15% bound' to '14.0% against 15%'. Restated on the metric the gate uses, aaMaxEffortGap 0.15 is 3.4x the A/A turns gap and strippedEffortMinMargin 0.25 is 5.7x it. Thresholds unchanged; the arithmetic behind them is now stated against the corrected data. strippedEffortMinMargin 0.25 is ~2.6x that widest A/A value; for scale the pilot's stripped arm came in at +6.3% on turns paired against A, with a 95% interval of [-17.1%, +29.7%] that straddles zero, so it would have failed both the margin and the interval test - which is the right answer, since that arm still solved 18/18. effortMetric is turns because it is an integer, it does not move with machine load (wall minutes) or verbosity (output tokens), and it was the quietest of the four across the A/A pair. (An earlier draft also said turns is what --max-turns counts; that is undocumented CLI-internal behaviour this repository cannot establish, so it is removed rather than asserted either way. The three reasons that remain do not depend on it.)

brick-baseline.$comment: BASELINE for the brick-house held-out task (2026-10-22): today's node vocabulary at ec145ab, three runs of one arm, so a later arm built after new grammar operators land (a box-split node, box names in the field grammar) can be run against the same task and compared. No gate: one arm has nothing to compare against, and the report's STOP 'gate arms not in the campaign' is expected. The task's brief carries three requirements beyond the corpus brick house (open holes, a door in each long wall, taller ground-storey windows) because graphs/examples-brick-house.json ships in this tarball and reaches the rest by params; see the task's CALIBRATION.md for what a copy scores.

brick-baseline-seeded.$comment: THE BASELINE OF RECORD for the brick vocabulary (2026-10-22), superseding brick-baseline: same arm, task brick-house-seeded. brick-baseline's first run solved its fixed-size brief with a 2-node graph that typed every box as a literal point list, which no grammar operator can make cheaper, so this task draws the footprint from the seed (14-18 x 10-14 studs, checked across 4 seeds) and the scorer, after an independent verification, ties every delivered brick to a packer's own output and requires openings to be empty through the wall. Re-run this campaign's task against a new arm to compare. No gate (one arm).

brick-ab-A.$comment: A/B of the split-grammar vocabulary (2026-10-22), arm A: the baseline vocabulary at ec145ab. Same task as brick-baseline-seeded (brick-house-seeded, selected by id), same prompt, model and effort, but the tarball is packed from a clean LF worktree of ec145ab and CUT WITH --strip-graphs, so the corpus house (graphs/examples-brick-house.json, which every baseline run opened) is not in the package; docs/graphs.{json,md} go with it, and the node docs keep only dangling example links. Arm B is campaign brick-ab-B: the same task, budgets and strip set against the grammar vocabulary. The two arms are separate campaigns only because B's commit did not exist when A started; they are run interleaved, one slot at a time (--max-slots 1). taskBudgets RAISE the task's 150 turns / 75 min for BOTH arms to 200 turns / 100 min and the output-token cap from 250k to 400k: the baseline's r0 used 130 of 150 turns with the corpus house to read, and an arm without it may cost more, so a capped run would measure the cap instead of the arm.

gate.label: none (one arm of a two-campaign A/B; compared by hand)

brick-ab-B.$comment: A/B of the split-grammar vocabulary (2026-10-22), arm B: the grammar vocabulary at d30ae215 (splitBox from c341678e, box names {"fn":"box","name":"x0"} / box("x0") from d30ae215). Everything but the tarball is brick-ab-A's: task brick-house-seeded by id, the same prompt, model, effort, taskBudgets (200 turns / 100 min / 400k output tokens) and strip set (--strip-graphs, the same three rules; it removes one entry more here, graphs/basics-split-box.json, the splitBox teaching graph that arm A never had). Packed from a clean LF worktree of d30ae215. Run interleaved with brick-ab-A, one slot at a time.

gate.label: none (one arm of a two-campaign A/B; compared by hand)
gate.$baselineArmsWhy: gate is merged over the defaults, whose baselineArms[0] is A; report.mjs pairs every arm against that and crashed on a campaign with no arm A. Set after slot r0, mirrored into this campaign's manifest.json gate (gate is not part of the campaign identity).

brick-ab-A-extra.$comment: ONE REPLACEMENT SLOT for brick-ab-A, whose r0 slot was contaminated on both attempts (a1 a classifier false positive, a2 a genuine `find / -maxdepth 1` listing of the Git install root) and so left the arm with 3 counted runs. Declared together with brick-ab-B-extra BEFORE either was run; counted whatever it scores, under the same contamination rules. Everything else is brick-ab-A's.

gate.label: none (replacement slot of a two-campaign A/B; compared by hand)

brick-ab-B-extra.$comment: ONE REPLACEMENT SLOT for brick-ab-B, whose r3 session was degenerate: at turn 1 the model wrote its first tool call as plain text ('Bash: Read brief.md ...') and ended the turn, without a tool call, without reading the brief (1 turn, 49 output tokens, no graph). The harness scores that as an unsolved final run; it measures nothing about either vocabulary. Declared together with brick-ab-A-extra BEFORE either was run; counted whatever it scores, under the same contamination rules. Everything else is brick-ab-B's.

gate.label: none (replacement slot of a two-campaign A/B; compared by hand)

estate-cal-A.$comment: Estate A/B (2026-10-23), CALIBRATION, arm A, NOT COUNTED: one run to set the counted caps. Library ec145ab7 (before splitBox, box names and applyRules), packed from a clean LF worktree with the e15e60b5 packer and stripped with its --strip-graphs (rewrites dangling corpus links, fails on any it misses). Task estate-division, its selftest graphs ported to the ec145ab7 vocabulary (build/port.mjs in the task). Generous caps (200 turns / 100 min / 400k output tokens) so the run measures the task, not the cap. building-calibration.$comment: CALIBRATION of the held-out task building-plan (2026-10-28), NOT an A/B: three runs on one arm, to measure what the task costs and whether agents reach for the box nodes when nothing else fits. Library f069b07b (main; the task's reference solves there and not on 50b2db89 or earlier, see the task's TASK-NOTES.md), packed from a clean LF worktree with the main checkout's packFromRepo and cut with --strip-graphs, as the facade-ab and estate-ab2 arms were, so graphs/examples-floorplan.json (the nearest corpus graph) is not in the package. Settings are facade-ab's: model and prompt from the defaults, the task's own 120 turns / 60 min with 250k output tokens set in taskBudgets, harness reschedules off (flags are read by hand). Not gate.mode calibration, which requires one run per task.

fixture.$comment: Exercises the runner end to end with the harness fixture task. Use with --agent evals/harness/fixtures/stub-agent.mjs --scorer evals/harness/fixtures/stub-score.mjs to spend no allowance.
